Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

around preposition and adverb

all round, round about a place

also round, round about, all around

classical

Ter. Heaut. 290–291: capillus passus, prōlixus, circum caput rejectus neglegenter
Verg. G. 2.523: dulcēs pendent circum ōscula nātī

circum (+ accusative)

preposition with the accusative; also an adverb

around, round (all round)

All the way round a thing: circum caput, round the head. Verbs repeat it: circumīre, go round; circumdare, put round, surround; circumspicere, look round.

Other words

  • circā (+ accusative) — around, round about; near

    preposition with the accusative; often an adverb · classical · Liv. 1.4.6: ex montibus quī circā sunt; Plin. Ep. 5.6.23: circā sipunculī plūrēs; Traupman 273

    Round about, in the neighbourhood: often an adverb, quī circā sunt, the people round about. Of times and numbers, about (Plin. Ep. 9.36.1: circā hōram prīmam).

  • circumeō, circumīre, circumiī, circumitum — go round, walk round

    verb, irregular (like eō), with the accusative, conjugation · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 9.33.4: nunc circumīre

Examples

  • capillus passus, prōlixus, circum caput rejectus neglegenter

    her hair loose, long, thrown carelessly round her headTer. Heaut. 290–291

  • intereā dulcēs pendent circum ōscula nātī

    meanwhile his sweet children hang round his neck for kissesVerg. G. 2.523

  • positōsque vernās, dītis exāmen domūs, circum renīdentīs Larīs

    and the home-born slaves, a rich house’s swarm, seated round the gleaming household godsHor. Epod. 2.65–66

  • fonticulus in hōc, in fonte crātēr; circā sipunculī plūrēs miscent jūcundissimum murmur

    in it a little spring, in the spring a basin; round it several little jets mingle a most pleasant murmurPlin. Ep. 5.6.23

  • delphīnus occurrit, et nunc praecēdere puerum nunc sequī nunc circumīre

    a dolphin met him, and now swam ahead of the boy, now behind him, now round himPlin. Ep. 9.33.4

  • suam quisque domum spatiō circumdat

    each of them surrounds his house with open groundTac. Germ. 16.2

See also round, between, throughout.
